THIS APPEAL & CROSS OBJECTION COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, RAJESH RAI K., J. DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 COMMON JUDGMENT

These, appeal and cross objection are arising out of the Judgment and award dated 30.06.2018 in MVC No.585/2015 passed by the Civil Judge (Sr. Dn.) and Addl.
MACT, Koppal (for short 'the Tribunal').
 2.

The brief facts of the case are that on 23.07.2015 at about 1.00 p.m., the deceased Syed Dada Aseempeer @ Hasimsab Makandar was returning on a motorcycle from Mundaragi by purchasing clothes and Kirani.

While he reached near Naala bridge of Murlapur at The Divisional Controller vs Sabira Banu W/O Late Syed Dada Aseempeer on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126406191/
4 Mundaragi-Murlapur road, at that time the respondent  -5-  MFA No. 103611 of 2018  C/W MFA.CROB No. 100031 of 2019 No.1 i.e. the driver of the NWKRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-26/F658 (respondent No.1) drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the two wheeler i.e. TVS moped of deceased.
Due to the said accident, the deceased Syed Dada Aseempeer @ Hasimsab fell on the road and sustained grievous injuries and died at the spot.
Hence, the claimants i.e. the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased filed claim petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act, in MVC No.585/2015 seeking compensation.
3. The claimants before the tribunal in order to prove their case, examined two witness i.e. P.W.1 and P.W.2 on their behalf and also got marked 14 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.

However, the respondent-KSRTC also examined one of his Officer as R.W.1 and got marked one document i.e. Ex.R.1 (photograph).
 4.

After hearing the learned counsel for both sides and appreciating the materials on record including the oral and documentary evidence, the tribunal allowed the claim  -6-  MFA No. 103611 of 2018  C/W MFA.CROB No. 100031 of 2019 The Divisional Controller vs Sabira Banu W/O Late Syed Dada Aseempeer on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126406191/
5 petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.16,32,000/- with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The tribunal directed respondent No.2 - NWKRTC to deposit the compensation within two months from the date of its order.

Aggrieved by the said Judgment and award,
NWKRTC filed the present appeal in MFA No.103611/2018 seeking to set aside the Judgment and award passed by the tribunal.
Nevertheless, the claimants also preferred cross objection in MFA Crob. No.100031/2019, seeking enhancement of the compensation amount.
5. We have heard the learned counsel from both sides i.e. for claimants as well for the NWKRTC.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant i.e. NWKRTC in MFA No.103611/2018, vehemently contended that, the Judgment and award of the tribunal is not sustainable either on law or on facts, since the tribunal has erred in fixing the liability on the NWRTKC, though the accident is a head on collusion between two vehicles, that too, in a
-7-  MFA No. 103611 of 2018  C/W MFA.CROB No. 100031 of 2019 curve road due to the sole negligence on the part of the deceased

. He would further contend that, the tribunal without perusing the oral evidence of R.W.1 i.e. the driver The Divisional Controller vs Sabira Banu W/O Late Syed Dada Aseempeer on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126406191/
6 of the bus and documentary evidence at Ex.R.1 i.e.
photograph and also Ex.P.14 the rough sketch of the spot of the accident, fixed the liability on the driver of the bus.

Ex.P.14 i.e. rough sketch would clearly indicate that the deceased drove his two wheeler in the middle of the road,
that too, in a curve, as such, the accident was caused due to the sole negligence of the deceased.
Hence, the tribunal is not justified in awarding compensation to the claimants.

He would further contend that, even otherwise the tribunal has erred in awarding excessive compensation and interest i.e. Rs.16,32,000/- with 7% interest per annum,
which is contrary to the law and facts and the evidence on record.
As such, learned counsel prays to set aside the award.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the claimants in MFA Crob, would contend that, the award passed by the  -8-  MFA No. 103611 of 2018  C/W MFA.CROB No. 100031 of 2019 tribunal does not suffer from any illegality and perversity and the same is as per the evidence available on record.
According to the learned counsel, the tribunal has rightly fixed the liability on the respondent i.e. driver of the NWKRTC bus by relying on the documents, especially the IMV report, marked at Ex.P.3 and also the charge-sheet submitted by the jurisdictional police as per Ex.P.6.

Those The Divisional Controller vs Sabira Banu W/O Late Syed Dada Aseempeer on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126406191/
7 documents clearly reveal that, due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending bus, the accident occurred.

sentences.text: According to Ex.P.16, i.e. the rough sketch of the spot of the incident, the accident took place in a curve road, to the extreme left side of the road where the deceased was riding and the driver of the bus without following the traffic rules came in a high speed and dashed to the motorcycle.
He would further contend that, even otherwise, the tribunal awarded a meager compensation under different heads without following the settled law.
As such, he prays to allow the cross objection and enhance the compensation.

We have bestowed our anxious consideration on the submissions made by both the parties and perused the materials available on record, including the trial Court records.

9. Having heard the learned counsels for both sides, and on perusal of the records, though the learned counsel for appellant-NWKRTC contended that, the accident was caused due to the negligent driving of the deceased, but on a cursory glance of the documents produced on behalf of the claimants i.e. complaint and FIR filed at the earliest point of time i.e. immediately after the The Divisional Controller vs Sabira Banu W/O Late Syed Dada Aseempeer on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126406191/
8 accident as per Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 then clearly depict that due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of NWKRTC bus, the accident was caused.

sentences.text: Moreover, even IMV report which marked as per Ex.P.3 clearly shows that, the accident was caused due to the negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus.
Accordingly, the police have filed charge-sheet as per Ex.P.6.
The said charge-sheet was not challenged by the respondent-corporation.

Even  - 10 -  MFA No. 103611 of 2018  C/W MFA.CROB No. 100031 of 2019 otherwise by perusal of Ex.P.14, the rough sketch of the spot clearly depicts that the accident was caused on the extreme left side of the road where the deceased was riding the two wheeler.

The NWKRTC bus was proceeding from Mundargi to Murlapur after crossing a curve, it is the duty of the driver of the bus to drive the vehicle to makeover the curve in a very slow manner by observing the traffic rules and regulations and more particularly, to look for the vehicles coming from opposite direction.

In that view of the matter, in our considered opinion, the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus, and the tribunal has rightly fixed the liability on the driver of the bus which was insured with the respondent No.2-Corporation.

10. Now insofar as the compensation awarded by The Divisional Controller vs Sabira Banu W/O Late Syed Dada Aseempeer on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126406191/
9

the tribunal is concerned, though the claimants have filed cross-objection seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the tribunal, the tribunal has rightly awarded compensation under different components except loss of  - 11 -  MFA No. 103611 of 2018  C/W MFA.CROB No. 100031 of 2019 consortium.
The tribunal has awarded only Rs.40,000/- for loss of consortium, whereas, there are five dependents to the deceased.

As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram reported on, 2018 reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the tribunal ought to have awarded Rs.40,000/- to each of the claimants i.e. on three heads i.e. spousal consortium,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

sentences.text: Hence, the tribunal has erred in awarding only Rs.40,000/- under the head of consortium.

Admittedly, the claim petition was filed by three children, wife and mother of the deceased,
and they all are entitle for Rs.40,000/- each which comes to Rs.2,00,000/-.
However, the tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- under the head of Funeral expenses and transportation of body, which is on higher side and it has to be reduced to Rs.15,000/-.

As contended by the learned counsel for the NWKRTC, the tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 7%, which is on higher side and it has to be reduced to 6%.

In the result, we pass the following:
 ORDER The Divisional Controller vs Sabira Banu W/O Late Syed Dada Aseempeer on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126406191/
11

In MFA No.103611/2018:
(i) Appeal filed by the NWKRC is allowed in part;
( ii) The compensation awarded under the head of funeral expenses and transportation of body of Rs.25,000/- is reduced to Rs.15,000/-.
(iii) Insofar as interest portion on the compensation is concerned, the same is reduced to 6%, instead of 7% as awarded by the tribunal.
(iv) The amount in deposit, if any, by the Insurance company shall be transmitted to the tribunal, forthwith.

In MFA Crob No.100031/2019:
(i) Cross objection filed by the claimants is also allowed in part;
(ii) The claimants are entitle for an additional compensation of - 14 - C/W MFA.CROB No. 100031 of 2019 Rs.1,10,000/- in addition to Rs.16,32,000/- as awarded by the tribunal, with 6% interest.
(i) The respondent No.2-NWKRTC
is directed to deposit the compensation amount within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
(ii) Registry is directed to return the trial Court records to the tribunal along with certified copy of the Judgment passed by this Court, without any delay.
(iii) No order as to costs.
